newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi Q1 growth on target-market.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi Q1 growth on target-market.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque Audi published its first quarter results on Tuesday and financiers said they were in line with the bank's forecast of 20 percent growth in profits for 1997.

Banque Audi reported quarterly net profits of 8.024 billion Lebanese pounds ($5.2 million) compared with 30.714 billion pounds for the whole of 1996. It gave no comparative figures for the first quarter of 1996 since it was not required to publish quarterly results before its January 20 listing on the Beirut Stock Exchange.
The bank's shares have appreciated 33 percent since they began trading on the exchange. Some financiers regard them as the re-emerging market's blue chip stock.
Market players were unconcerned that the first quarter results were not mathematically in line with the 20 percent target.

"If you take into account that this is traditionally the worst quarter for profits, they are in line with the forecast 20 percent growth," Georges Abou Jaoude, director of Lebanese operations at Financial Funds Advisers, a Beirut finance house, told Reuters.

"The results are as expected, roughly 20 percent growth, which is what has been talked about on the market," said Ziad Makawi, director for capital markets at Middle East Capital Group (MECG) finance house.
(Corrects institution in which Makawi works from Lebanon Invest)
Makawi calculated Audi's earnings per share on the basis of the results at $1.70, which he said was in line with market expectations. This put the price/earnings ratio at 11.75, he added.
"In general, earnings are as expected. Personally, I think we are going to see very strong appreciation of all bank stocks," he said.

Of the other two banks listed on the exchange, Bank of Beirut reported first quarter profits up 29.6 percent on April 21 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce is due to issue its quarterly results by the end of the month.
Financiers said BLC growth was also expected to be on target.

Shares in a fourth bank, Byblos Bank, which is expected to list on the Beirut Stock Exchange in June, are currently traded on the grey or parallel market. Traders say they are in heavy demand and have risen rapidly to a current level of $6.5-$7.00.
